# Hexaequo

> A free abstract strategy board game for two players, played in a web browser.
> There is no fixed board: the players build it as they play, laying hexagonal
> tiles and moving two kinds of piece. No dice, no hidden information, no
> account required, no advertising.

Hexaequo is played on a board that does not exist at the start. Each player has
9 tiles, 6 disks and 3 rings. On your turn you do exactly one of three things:
lay a tile, place a piece from your reserve, or move a piece already on the
board. A disk steps to a neighbouring tile or jumps over a piece, capturing it,
and may chain several jumps in one turn. A ring leaps to any tile two spaces
away and captures whatever it lands on. You win by capturing six enemy disks,
three enemy rings, or by leaving your opponent with no piece on the board.

It can be played by two people on one device, against a computer opponent at
four strengths, or online — by invitation link, or as a rated game matched by
rating, with clocks and a leaderboard. It installs to a phone home screen and
works offline. Created by Piero Barrette.

## Pages

- [Play Hexaequo](https://hexaequo.com/play/): what the game is, how it is
  played, and the four ways to play it.
- [Rules](https://hexaequo.com/rules/): the complete rules, in full.
- [Jouer à Hexaequo](https://hexaequo.com/fr/jouer/): the same in French.
- [Règles](https://hexaequo.com/fr/regles/): the complete rules in French.
- [The game itself](https://hexaequo.com/): the playable application.
